description: Tab strip component with Line, Pill, and Enclosed visual variants. Supports icons, badges, disabled tabs, and keyboard arrow-key navigation. Use with TmTabPanel children. Since TG-007 (2.11.0) the tab strip follows the interface density contract: inside a data-tm-density="compact" ancestor the row padding is re-metered for every variant (Line row 42 px -> 34 px); the variant chrome (tray, borders, radii) is untouched and comfortable (no attribute) is unchanged.

parameters.name: AriaLabel
parameters.description: Accessible name of the tablist. Null leaves the strip unnamed.

parameters.name: ActiveTabId
parameters.description: ID of the currently active tab.

parameters.name: ActiveTabIdChanged
parameters.description: Fires when the active tab changes.

parameters.name: Variant
parameters.description: Visual variant of the tab strip.

parameters.name: Wrap
parameters.description: When true, the tab strip wraps onto multiple rows to fit the available width instead of scrolling horizontally. Kept for compatibility: the same layout is reachable through Overflow = TabsOverflow.Wrap. The effective layout wraps when EITHER the flag is set OR Overflow is Wrap. Prefer Overflow; when both are set, Wrap wins.

parameters.name: Overflow
parameters.description: How the strip behaves when the tabs do not fit the available width — Scroll (default; the historical one-row horizontal scroll, now with token-coloured edge shadows over the clipped tabs) or Wrap (multiple rows; the layout of the legacy Wrap boolean). The root gets tm-tabs--wrap in Wrap mode; Scroll mode adds no class (it is styled through .tm-tabs:not(.tm-tabs--wrap)).

parameters.name: StickyHeader
parameters.description: When true, the tab strip sticks to the top of its nearest scrolling ancestor while the content scrolls under it. The offset is the --tm-tabs-sticky-top token (default 0, e.g. 56px to clear a fixed app bar). With header slots in use the ROW (.tm-tabs__header-row) is what sticks, matching the sticky-consumer contract of HeaderLeading. Renders the tm-tabs--sticky class.

parameters.name: IdPrefix
parameters.description: Opt-in id prefix that scopes the generated DOM ids ({prefix}-tab-{id} / {prefix}-tabpanel-{id}) so two TmTabs instances can carry the same panel ids without colliding. Null (default) keeps the global tab-{id} / tabpanel-{id} schema.

parameters.name: KeepInactivePanels
parameters.description: When true, EVERY tab panel is rendered and the inactive ones carry the hidden attribute, so hosts keep state (input drafts, scroll positions, canvas measurements) alive across tab switches. Default false keeps the historical lazy rendering: only the active panel exists, and aria-controls then points at the active panel only — a tab must never reference a panel that is not in the DOM.

parameters.name: HeaderLeading
parameters.description: Optional content rendered immediately BEFORE the tab strip, as a SIBLING of the role="tablist" element — never inside it. The tab strip owns a roving tabindex (Arrow/Home/End, tabindex 0/-1, aria-selected AND the DOM focus, which moves with the selection); an element that can never be selected would misreport that contract to assistive technology and would be reachable with the arrow keys as if it were a tab. Setting this (or HeaderTrailing) wraps the strip in an extra .tm-tabs__header-row flex row. The wrapper is emitted ONLY when at least one slot is supplied; with neither slot the rendered markup is byte-identical to a tab strip that has no slots at all, so existing CSS and tests that rely on .tm-tabs > .tm-tabs__header keep working. CONTRACT FOR STICKY CONSUMERS: when the slots are in use, a sticky tab strip must stick the ROW (.tm-tabs__header-row), not the header (.tm-tabs__header). Sticking the header alone pins only the strip and lets the slot content scroll away.

parameters.name: HeaderTrailing
parameters.description: Optional content rendered immediately AFTER the tab strip, as a SIBLING of the role="tablist" element — never inside it, for the same roving-focus reason as HeaderLeading. Setting this (or HeaderLeading) wraps the strip in an extra .tm-tabs__header-row flex row. The wrapper is emitted ONLY when at least one slot is supplied; with neither slot the rendered markup is byte-identical to a tab strip that has no slots at all. CONTRACT FOR STICKY CONSUMERS: when the slots are in use, stick the ROW (.tm-tabs__header-row), not the header (.tm-tabs__header), otherwise the slot content scrolls away from under the pinned strip.

cssVariables.name: --tm-tabs-sticky-top
cssVariables.description: Offset from the top of the scrolling ancestor for StickyHeader (default 0, e.g. 56px to clear a fixed app bar). Declared on :root, so a host override on :root or any wrapper ancestor wins.

cssVariables.name: --tm-tabs-scroll-cover
cssVariables.description: Colour the scroll-mode edge-shadow covers (and the sticky strip background) paint. Defaults to --tm-bg-surface; Pill re-declares it to --tm-bg-muted. A host whose strip sits on another background re-declares the token to that background.

cssVariables.name: --tm-tabs-edge-shadow-size
cssVariables.description: Width of each scroll-mode edge-shadow band (gradient fade and background-size). Defaults to var(--tm-space-4) = 16px.
